result.title: A Novel Federated Learning Framework for Defending Against Gradient Inversion Attacks
result.summary: Federated Learning (FL) offers a paradigm for collaborative machine learning model training among clients, preserving data privacy by avoiding direct data sharing. However, the gradient information exchanged in FL has been shown to be vulnerable to Gradient Inversion Attacks (GIA), which can reconstruct sensitive user data. To counter these threats, various privacy-enhancing technologies like Secure Multi-party Computing (SMC), Homomorphic Encryption (HE), and Differential Privacy (DP) have been integrated into FL. While effective, these methods often introduce significant trade-offs between privacy and model utility. By revisiting the key to privacy exposure in FL under GIA, which lies in the frequent sharing of model gradients that contain private data, we take a new perspective by designing a novel privacy-preserving FL framework that effectively ``breaks the direct connection'' between the shared parameters and the local private data to defend against GIA. Our proposed framework, HyperFL++, leverages hypernetworks to generate local model parameters, where only the hypernetwork parameters are aggregated by the server. To ensure practicality, HyperFL++ incorporates a Row-wise Kronecker Decomposition (RKD) to mitigate the memory and communication overhead from the hypernetwork. Comprehensive theoretical analysis and extensive experiments validate our method's effectiveness in protecting data privacy while maintaining high model utility. Our code is available at https://github.com/Pengxin-Guo/HyperFL/tree/hyperfl%2B%2B.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 HyperFL++ 联邦学习框架，用超网络生成客户端本地模型参数、仅聚合超网络参数以切断共享参数与本地私有数据的直接联系，并用行式 Kronecker 分解降低额外开销，以抵御梯度反演攻击。
AI.relevance_reason: 主题为联邦学习的隐私保护与通信/存储效率，未涉及视觉或多模态推理状态、证据获取或 latent 推理过程，超网络的参数生成也不构成可供核查的 LVR 方法线索。
